decisions.rationale: "Myotonic dystrophy" in the title names one specific disease (DM) with no further categorization.
Repeat mention of "Myotonic dystrophy" in the abstract refers to the same specific disease and is annotated again as a duplicate.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §4 - Annotate duplicate mentions

decisions.rationale: "DM" is the abbreviation defined for Myotonic dystrophy, so it is a separate mention for the short form referring to the same specific disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §6 - Abbreviation definitions annotated as separate mentions

decisions.rationale: "neuromuscular disorder" describes a family of multiple specific diseases rather than one specific disease, so it is a Disease Class.
Here "DM" is the name of the DM gene ("the DM gene"), not a disease mention, so it is not annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 - only disease mentions are annotated

decisions.rationale: "disease" is a very general term and is excluded from annotation.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate §4 - Do not annotate general terms

decisions.rationale: "congenital form" refers to a particular form of myotonic dystrophy (congenital myotonic dystrophy), which corresponds to one specific disease, similar to the classical galactosemia example.
decisions.guideline_section: Examples §15 - Form of disease corresponding to a particular form counts as Specific Disease

decisions.rationale: "DM" is used as a modifier of "tissues" in "various DM tissues", so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §3 - Disease mentions used as Modifiers

decisions.rationale: "DM" modifies the noun "patients" in "418 DM patients", so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §3 - Disease mentions used as Modifiers

decisions.rationale: Second occurrence of "congenital form" refers to the congenital form of myotonic dystrophy, a specific disease form, so it is annotated consistently with candidate 7.
decisions.guideline_section: Examples §15 - Form of disease corresponding to a particular form counts as Specific Disease
